SCIENTIFIC-DATA-ANALYSIS
Release v2.2 evaluation-hardening / v2.1 compact-router / v2.0 integrated skill + ScientificWorkbench / v1.9 contract-freeze / v1.8 app-ready backend / v1.7 real-world / v1.6 stable baseline

Compatibility anchors for historical gates: Release v1.7 stable / v1.6 stable baseline; v1.7 is the installed stable.

What this release means:
- The core scope is defined and documented.
- The runtime is quieter and more reproducible than in earlier iterations.
- The product layer is more polished, with more consistent outputs and cleaner handoff bundles.
- The installation story is now explicit for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
- The environment doctor can distinguish core readiness from optional extras.
- The skill remains science-first, especially for astronomy and technical analysis.
- v2.0 aligns the installed skill with ScientificWorkbench as a native macOS product surface: the app reads the installed public registry, executes the skill through deterministic commands, consumes JSON envelopes and run bundles, displays typed artifacts and previews, tracks job state, and preserves controlled `WARNING`/`BLOCKED_CONTROLADO` outcomes.
- The stable base now includes explicit cross-domain workflows for mixed tables and mixed document intake.
- The stable base now also includes compact photometric-calibration and detector-noise planning helpers inspired by standard photometry and detector texts, without turning the core into an oversized instrument package.
- The stable base now also includes a narrower golden path for reduced ASCII spectra, existing notebooks, and coursework-style reports.
- The validation path now also exercises those cross-domain workflows plus reusable non-science deliverable scaffolds.
- The skill now ships with `deploy/` wrappers, packaged `examples/`, and a portable smoke test for moving it to other machines more safely.
- Privacy-sensitive runtime details in normal JSON outputs are now sanitized more aggressively for safer sharing and publication.
- TEAREDUCE is now consolidated as an optional backend with four practical routes (`bias`, `flat`, `cr2images`, `wavecalib`) plus a dedicated short smoke-test wrapper.
- The `datanalysis` contract is more honest now: it explicitly validates notebook runtime pieces such as `plotly`, `nbclient`, and kernel execution, while distinguishing a restricted sandbox from a broken environment.
- Post-audit hardening adds focused regressions, Li ASCII EW support, clearer failed-input behavior, and standard JSON envelopes for several supporting tools without changing the skill's core shape.
- v1.2 closes the recent coursework and document-handoff maturation: professor-notebook fidelity, Pages/DOCX marked edits, macOS PDF fallback, exact visual handoff, and a focused v1.2 release regression gate.
- v1.3 closes the full-capability audit follow-up without changing the architecture: DuckDB skips unsafe stem aliases such as `table`, the SB2 public `fit` command works, legacy RV input validation emits blocked JSON, and the reduced ASCII spectra coursework route passes the full smoke path again.
- v1.4 adds companion routing without changing the scientific architecture: `companion_route_check.py` recommends local installed companion skills/plugins for narrow handoff steps while keeping email, Google Drive, and Zotero outside this release's routing policy.
- The post-v1.4 astronomy route now adds a narrow FITS RGB batch helper for derived visual products: grouped FITS inventory, per-filter stacks, WCS-aware channel alignment, pseudo-RGB labeling, manifests, and alignment QA.
- The optional external astronomy route now adds controlled bridges for STILTS/TOPCAT and Aperture Photometry Tool: explicit preflight, reproducible commands, logs, manifests, APT source-list preparation, and APT output parsing without making Java tools mandatory.
- v1.5 closes the capability-coverage loop: `capability_probe_matrix.py` now probes every public `smoke none` entry that is safe to exercise, including visual RGB FITS export, and `audit_v1_5_release_regression.py` rejects real failures or unprobed public entries.
- Historical marker: Release v1.5 stable is the capability-coverage baseline that v1.6 audits and hardens.
- v1.6 closes the 59-capability audit pass generated from `Capacidades scientific-data-analysis v1.6.pdf`: every public registry entry was exercised through happy, realistic, edge, and broken cases where applicable; accepted P0/P1/P2 fixes were retested; and each phase closure synced editable changes into the installed skill only after validation.
- v1.7 is the installed stable real-world applicability release. Its focus is classification of all public capabilities, non-astro intake, measurement/noise/QA transfer, astronomy-born pattern boundaries, professional/personal package playbooks, and a user-facing v1.7 guide.
- v1.8 is the app-ready backend release: JSON envelopes, run-bundle contract, app-readiness matrix, dry-run router, app-like regressions, and a clear boundary that ScientificWorkbench sync remains future work.
- v1.9 is the stable contract-freeze and app-facing hardening release: artifact type names are frozen, app-facing errors are cleaner, app hints and next actions are richer, exposure modes are locked, v2.0 deferrals are protected, and app-like regression coverage is broader.
- v2.0 is the installed integrated release when post-sync validation passes: the ScientificWorkbench app is validated against the installed skill path, parser/artifact/job-history/workflow tests pass, and packaged/headless app smokes run against the same skill contract.
- v2.1 is the compact-router release: SKILL.md stays short while generated surface details and historical routing live in references.
- v2.2 is the evaluation-hardening release: plugin-eval baseline findings are addressed by keeping transient outputs and generated caches out of the active bundle, replacing bulky historical routing with a compatibility stub, expanding visible regression wrappers, and updating the guide to v2.2 without changing the registry or ScientificWorkbench.

What this release does promise:
- A stable core stack for FITS, tables, notebooks, documents, LaTeX, copied presentations, and reproducible handoffs.
- A stable core path for first-order photometric calibration and detector/SNR planning.
- A stable core path for reduced ASCII spectra plus existing notebooks and final coursework bundles.
- Reusable cross-domain paths for operational tabular review and document intake without touching originals.
- Graceful degradation when optional tools are missing.
- A portable installation path using requirements-core.txt, requirements-full.txt, or environment.yml.
- A doctor script for checking machine readiness.
- More consistent summaries, manifests, handoff indexes, and copied-deck bundles.
- A tested v1.2 route for professor-provided notebooks: input() handling, sidecar checks, question/answer mapping, Plotly portability, static fallback warnings, and cleanup policy.
- A tested v1.2 route for documents and presentations: Pages-exported DOCX marked-fragment edits, PDF visual fallback on macOS, scientific asset manifests, and exact visual-equivalent handoff.
- A tested v1.3 capability-hardening route for the concrete audit failures found while exercising every public entrypoint.
- A tested v1.4 companion-routing route for local handoffs to pdf, document, presentation, spreadsheet, notebook, browser/visual, screenshot, audio, image, and frontend companions when they are justified.
- A narrow, tested FITS RGB batch route for visual products when a tree of multiband FITS images needs reproducible PNGs, stacks, manifests, and alignment reports.
- A controlled optional route for STILTS catalog conversion/filtering/sky crossmatch/VOTable validation and APT batch photometry handoff when those Java tools are installed and configured.
- A tested v1.5 capability-coverage route for public capabilities without direct smoke tests, with controlled `WARNING`/`BLOCKED_CONTROLADO` outcomes separated from real `FAIL` states.
- A tested v1.6 hardening route for all 59 public capabilities, with final phase closures validated in both the editable and installed skill trees.
- A v1.7 stable documentation route that explains which capabilities are general, cross-domain adaptable, domain-specific, legacy-specific, or maintainer-only, with examples for academic, professional, and personal use.
- Explicit not-applicable criteria so narrow astronomy, legacy, or maintainer tools are not marketed as general-purpose tools.
- A v1.8/v1.9/v2.0 backend and app contract route: stable envelopes, typed artifacts, run bundles, app hints, next actions, error kinds, exposure modes, job metadata, app-side previews, and dual release gates spanning the installed skill plus ScientificWorkbench.

What this release does not promise:
- Perfect parity across all operating systems for every helper.
- Full GUI-equivalent behavior for every proprietary format.
- TEAREDUCE availability by default.
- Observatory-grade instrument-specific pipelines out of the box.
- Full CCD reduction or calibration verification inside the RGB batch helper; it labels uncertain calibration state rather than pretending it is solved.
- STILTS, TOPCAT, APT, Java, or APT preferences availability by default.
- Hidden automation of TOPCAT or APT GUI sessions.
- Automatic privacy review of user-authored content inside external datasets or reports.
- Automatic use of email, Google Drive, or Zotero from the skill's companion-routing layer.

Short TEAREDUCE note:
- Use `deploy/run-teareduce-smoke.sh` or `deploy/run-teareduce-smoke.ps1` for the shortest end-to-end TEAREDUCE health check.
- The consolidated TEAREDUCE smoke test now validates the four practical routes together on this machine.
